candidates.downstream_effects: Identical HIGH/LOW pulse every time, regardless of caller or system state. No conditional branch inside FUN_00006952 itself -- it takes no parameters and cannot vary its output.

candidates.known_firmware_role: Pulsed HIGH for ~50ms (both pins together) only inside the two byte-identical motor-driver disable sequences (FUN_000077f8 / FUN_00007868), immediately before the enable pins (PB16/PB17) are finally driven LOW.
upstream_causes: sketch_loop__CUSTOM's own motor-connector-presence poll (NEW this pass): reads a per-channel presence-detect GPIO pair for all 4 channels every main-loop iteration; when the aggregate connected/disconnected pattern changes from the previous scan, calls FUN_00007868 (if going from 'some connected' to 'none connected') or FUN_000077a0/enable (the re-detected case) -- this is the firmware side of the manual's documented 'AutoPilot auto-detects which of the four ports have a motor connected' behavior

ascii_dispatcher__CUSTOM, ASCII command 'J' (0x4A) (NEW this pass): under two mutually-exclusive sub-condition flags, reaches either FUN_00007868 or FUN_000077f8. This is a previously-undocumented wire-command link -- 'J' is not yet named/characterized elsewhere in docs/protocol/*.
candidates.downstream_effects: ~50ms HIGH pulse on PB06/PB07, then PB16/PB17 (enable) driven LOW, ending the motor-driver enable state. Re-enable (PB16/PB17 HIGH) is separately reachable from the same main-loop presence poll, from ASCII command 'J' 's counterpart path, and from inbound F0/E0 manual-jog frames (ascii_dispatcher, 0x8274/0x82d6 -- reached only when a 'was disabled' condition flag is set).
candidates.physical_meaning: Still not independently confirmed as reset vs. strobe -- this pass adds WHEN it fires (real, meaningful preconditions) but not WHAT it electrically does on the driver IC, which needs the exact driver-IC datasheet, out of reach of any tool used here.

candidates.known_firmware_role: TCC1's own IRQ handler (0x60ec, IRQ93) does an inline PORT.GROUP1.OUTTGL toggle of PB22 -- already known. This candidate's CONFIGURATION, ENABLE/DISABLE lifecycle, and runtime firing were all resolved by this pass, the second half concretely (see TCC1/PB22 Boot Runtime Replay).
upstream_causes: FUN_00005570(param_1), a per-peripheral configuration function with a switch on param_1: cases 0/1/2/3 configure TC0-TC3's own EIC/PORT setup; case 7 configures TCC1 specifically (CTRLA=0x100, a prescaler/mode write -- NOT the ENABLE bit; PER=0x20000000; CC0=0x10000). Called with values 0,1,2,3,7 (5 total calls) EXCLUSIVELY from FUN_00006968, the startup reference/input boot routine. CONCRETELY CONFIRMED in the boot replay at instruction 65062-65071 (CTRLA=0x100, offset+0x3c=1, CC0=0x10000) -- exact match to the static prediction.

The only OTHER caller path into FUN_00005570 is FUN_00005f8c, itself called from FUN_00006338 (phase-2/3 monitor, x2) and ascii_dispatcher__CUSTOM (x1) -- all with per-channel arguments in the 0-3 range (motor-channel re-arm), never observed reaching case 7. No live/wire-command path to TCC1's own configuration was found.

CONCRETELY IDENTIFIED this pass (Boot Runtime Replay): the real ENABLE writer is FUN_00005d24 (CTRLA=0x102, ENABLE bit genuinely set), NOT FUN_0000434c as the earlier static pass's phrasing implied. FUN_00005d24 is called exclusively from inside FUN_00005d44 -- the already-documented 'dead' 128-sample ADC-baseline boot function, NOT the reference-seek move. TCC1 was enabled/disabled twice, both pairs entirely inside FUN_00005d44's own execution window (instr 251605-259661 and 263738-271782 of a 450,000-instruction replay), immediately on that function's entry and again before its return.
candidates.downstream_effects: FUN_0000434c explicitly DISABLES TCC1 (clears CTRLA.ENABLE, confirmed by the replay: CTRLA read then written back as 0x100) and drives PB22 LOW via its own digitalWrite call -- both concretely observed, twice, exactly bracketing FUN_00005d44's two enabled intervals. Also called from loop_housekeeping_save_trigger__CUSTOM's power-button-held halt sequence (not exercised in this boot-only replay). ACROSS THE FULL 450,000-INSTRUCTION REPLAY (11 real main-loop iterations past steady state): TCC1's IRQ handler (0x60ec) was watched and hit ZERO times; PORT.GROUP1.OUTTGL (0x4100809c) was never written once. The only PB22 MMIO activity observed was the initial pinMode(OUTPUT)+digitalWrite(LOW) during boot config and FUN_0000434c's own two explicit LOW writes -- never a toggle.
candidates.physical_meaning: UNKNOWN which physical function PB22 drives. The earlier co-configuration-timing inference ('tied to the reference-seek move') is now SUPERSEDED by the concrete finding that TCC1's actual enable/disable activity is bracketed entirely within the ADC-baseline function instead -- which that same function's own outputs are already documented elsewhere as unconsumed/dead, raising the possibility this TCC1 usage is likewise functionally inert on this firmware, not merely unidentified.
